RS/390/CC/NOTICE/ACP/DHL/2023 ISSUED BY THE R5 STATING THAT AS PER PERMISSION DATED 29/12/2023 IN KARNATAKA POLICE MUNAL ORDER NO. 1059(5) TO OPEN THE A ROWDY SHEET AGAINST THE PETITIONER AT ANNEXURE-A AND ALSO TO QUASH THE POLICE NOTICE DATED 05/12/2023 VIDE NO. 2 the Police notice dated 05.12.2023 vide NO.CJ/PS/CC/___/2023 issued by the 6th Respondent to open the Rowdy sheet against the Petitioner, at "Annexure - B."
iv.

Call for the records in all three criminal cases in Crime No.19/2015 for the offences under section 143, 447, 427, 323, 506 R/W 149 of IPC, Crime No.142/2017 for the offences under section 143, 447,
506, 323, 420 and 149 of IPC, and Crime No. 115/2023 for the offences under section 420, 465, 468,
469, 471 of IPC by the Chikkajala Police Station/6th Respondent; ii. Grant such other and further reliefs as this Hon'ble Tribunal deems to grant under the circumstances of the case."
2.
Heard Sri. Vijaya Kumar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri. Manjunath, learned HCGP appearing for the respondents.
3. The petitioner gets embroiled in three crimes; one in Crime No.19/2015 for offences punishable under Sections 143, 447, 427, 323 and 506 of the IPC.
The petitioner gets acquitted by an order of the competent Court.
The acquittal has become final.

The petitioner again gets embroiled in another NC: 2024:KHC:2194 crime in Crime No.142/2017 for offences punishable under Sections 143, 447,
506, 323, 420 and 149 of the IPC.
The offences are verbatim similar to what was alleged in Crime No.19/2015.
The police themselves dropped the name of the petitioner while filing the charge sheet.
The third crime, in which, the petitioner is now an accused is Crime No.115/2023, which is in the stage of investigation.
4. The issue in the lis does not concern the merit of the crime in Crime No.115/2023.

What has driven the petitioner to this Court in the subject petition is a notice issued by the competent authority seeking to show cause as to why the name of the petitioner should not be drawn/continued in the list of rowdies before the Chikkajala Police Station - respondent No.6.
5.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would take this Court through the documents appended to the petition contending that the police notice was issued on 05.12.2023 and the petitioner has replied on 13.12.2023 explaining every content of the notice.
Notwithstanding the same, a notice is issued which is impugned in the petition.
He would seek quashment of the notice and grant of all consequential benefits.

Learned HCGP on the other hand would submit that a crime is pending investigation in Crime No.115/2023 and it is immaterial, if the petitioner is acquitted in other crimes as on the date of issuance of notice.
He would submit that drawing up of persons in the list of rowdies need not be pursuant to registration of crime.

If they are miscreants in the vicinity in terms of the police manual,
the name of those persons can be drawn in the list of rowdies.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the respective submissions made by the learned counsel and have perused the material on record.

sentences.text: The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute.
The crimes against the petitioner were 3 in number, in one, the petitioner gets acquitted, the acquittal has become final.

In the second, the police themselves have dropped the name of the petitioner from the array of accused while filing the charge sheet, what remains is Crime No.115/2023 for offences punishable under Sections 420, 465,
468, 469 and 471 of the IPC.

The notice issued on 05.12.2023 is replied to by the petitioner on 13.12.202 bringing it to the notice of respondent No.6 that there is no case worth the name pending for drawing NC: 2024:KHC:2194 up the name of the petitioner in the list of rowdies.
It is therefore his submission that it should be quashed.

9. Since it is only a notice that is issued to the petitioner and the petitioner is to reply seeking show cause why it cannot be done, the reply be submitted by the petitioner to the notice dated 29.12.2023.

The reply shall merit consideration at the hands of respondent No.6 strictly in consonance with what the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court has held in W.P.No.4504/2021 and connected matters disposed on 22.04.2022.
The Co-ordinate Bench lays down certain guidelines.

The guidelines so laid down by the Co-ordinate Bench reads as follows:
GUIDELINES FOR ROWDY/HISTORY SHEETING:
i. Before entering the name of an individual to the Register of Rowdies, the jurisdictional police shall collect and collate the material information concerning him and frame the proposal for registration on that basis.

ii. A brief proposal notice shall be sent to the individual concerned in a sealed cover with an option to submit his representation within two weeks as to why his name should not be registered as a rowdy.
However, there is no need to afford a personal hearing.
In exceptional cases notice may be dispensed with for reasons to be recorded in the Register of Rowdies.

iii. In terms of Clause (5), Order 1059 of the Manual, the Superintendent of Police or the Sub - Divisional Police Officer shall not accord approval for entering the name of individual concerned to the Register of Rowdies without calling for records and objectively considering the same.

He shall briefly record his reasons for according the NC: 2024:KHC:2194 approval and mark a copy thereof to the individual forthwith,
with a mention that he may petition the Police Complaints Authority, against the same.
iv. The jurisdictional Police shall compulsorily once in two years, undertake a periodic review of entries in the Register of Rowdies suo motu, as provided under Clause (2), Order 1057 of the Manual.

However, it is open to the aggrieved, to make a representation at any time after one year of registration, seeking deletion of name from the Rowdy Register on the basis of changed circumstances such as rectitude,
good conduct, social/community service, etc. v.

The representation for review shall be considered by the jurisdictional Police at the initial level within a period of 30 days, during which necessary inputs may be obtained through the available sources as to merits of the claim.

sentences.text: The recommendation shall be sent to the jurisdictional Superintendent of Police or the Sub - Divisional Police Officer, within 15 days along with the representation & the material collected thereon.
Such recommendation along with the result of consideration of the representation shall be communicated to the individual concerned within next 15 days.
vi. Any individual aggrieved by the rejection of his representation or continuation of his name in the Register may petition to the Police Complaints Authority ordinarily within 30 days.
However, no personal hearing shall avail.
The petition shall be disposed off by recording reasons within an outer limit of 60 days, after considering the material on record or the fresh inputs that may be requisitioned, by the authority.

vii. The entire process of Rowdy/History Sheeting from the stage of issuance of proposal notice as specified above, up to the issuance of the orders on the petition if any to the Police Complaints Authority, shall be done only in a sealed cover procedure and that nothing therein shall be disclosed nor made available to anyone, except to the aggrieved, nor any Right To Information (RTI)
application shall be entertained in this regard.
viii.

The violation of these guidelines shall constitute a major misconduct and an adverse entry on proof thereof shall be made by the Disciplinary Authority in the Service Register of the erring official after hearing him and a copy thereof shall be marked to the victim of Rowdy Register/History Sheet,
without brooking any delay.

Whatever guidelines herein above laid down shall be applicable to the case of History Sheeters as well, mutatis mutandis and subject to the provisions of Karnataka Police Manual, 1965.
10.

Therefore, respondent No.6 - the Assistant Commissioner of Police shall consider the reply submitted or that would be submitted by the petitioner to the notice so issued, and pass appropriate orders bearing in mind the observations made in the course of the order, as also the law laid down by the Co-ordinate Bench quoted supra.
11.
Till such time, i.e., the consideration of the reply to the petitioner happens, the respondents shall not precipitate the matter.
With the aforesaid observations, the petition stands disposed.

9. Since it is only a notice that is issued to the petitioner and the petitioner is to reply seeking show cause why it cannot be done, the reply be submitted by the petitioner to the notice dated 29.12.2023.
The reply shall merit consideration at the hands of respondent No.6 strictly in consonance with what the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court has held in W.P.No.4504/2021 and connected matters disposed on 22.04.2022.
He shall briefly record his reasons for according the NC: 2024:KHC:2194 approval and mark a copy thereof to the individual forthwith,
with a mention that he may petition the Police Complaints Authority, against the same.
iv. The jurisdictional Police shall compulsorily once in two years, undertake a periodic review of entries in the Register of Rowdies suo motu, as provided under Clause (2), Order 1057 of the Manual.
However, it is open to the aggrieved, to make a representation at any time after one year of registration, seeking deletion of name from the Rowdy Register on the basis of changed circumstances such as rectitude,
good conduct, social/community service, etc. v.
The representation for review shall be considered by the jurisdictional Police at the initial level within a period of 30 days, during which necessary inputs may be obtained through the available sources as to merits of the claim.
The recommendation shall be sent to the jurisdictional Superintendent of Police or the Sub - Divisional Police Officer, within 15 days along with the representation & the material collected thereon.
Such recommendation along with the result of consideration of the representation shall be communicated to the individual concerned within next 15 days.
vi. Any individual aggrieved by the rejection of his representation or continuation of his name in the Register may petition to the Police Complaints Authority ordinarily within 30 days.
However, no personal hearing shall avail.
The petition shall be disposed off by recording reasons within an outer limit of 60 days, after considering the material on record or the fresh inputs that may be requisitioned, by the authority.
vii. The entire process of Rowdy/History Sheeting from the stage of issuance of proposal notice as specified above, up to the issuance of the orders on the petition if any to the Police Complaints Authority, shall be done only in a sealed cover procedure and that nothing therein shall be disclosed nor made available to anyone, except to the aggrieved, nor any Right To Information (RTI)
application shall be entertained in this regard.
viii.
The violation of these guidelines shall constitute a major misconduct and an adverse entry on proof thereof shall be made by the Disciplinary Authority in the Service Register of the erring official after hearing him and a copy thereof shall be marked to the victim of Rowdy Register/History Sheet,
without brooking any delay.
NC: 2024:KHC:2194 ix.
Whatever guidelines herein above laid down shall be applicable to the case of History Sheeters as well, mutatis mutandis and subject to the provisions of Karnataka Police Manual, 1965.
10.
Therefore, respondent No.6 - the Assistant Commissioner of Police shall consider the reply submitted or that would be submitted by the petitioner to the notice so issued, and pass appropriate orders bearing in mind the observations made in the course of the order, as also the law laid down by the Co-ordinate Bench quoted supra.
11.
Till such time, i.e., the consideration of the reply to the petitioner happens, the respondents shall not precipitate the matter.
With the aforesaid observations, the petition stands disposed.
